record.original_question: For a k-orbit abstract polytope—meaning an abstract polytope whose automorphism group has k orbits on flags—suppose one is given a distinguished generating set for its automorphism group analogous to the standard generators used for regular polytopes. What condition on those generators should replace the string C-group intersection condition so that the generator data still captures the polytope structure?

evidence.quote: Problem 1. Given a distinguished generating set for the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope, what analogue of the intersection condition holds?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
An abstract n-polytope is a partially ordered set with a rank function whose elements (called faces) of ranks 0,...,n-1 satisfy the standard axioms generalizing the face lattice of a convex polytope: it has a unique minimum face and a unique maximum face, every maximal chain (flag) contains exactly n+2 elements, the poset is strongly flag-connected, and the diamond condition holds (for any face F of rank i-1 and any face G of rank i+1 with F<G, there are exactly two faces H of rank i with F<H<G). The automorphism group Γ(P) acts freely on the set of flags. The polytope P is called a k-orbit polytope if Γ(P) has exactly k orbits on flags.

For a regular abstract n-polytope (the case k=1), fixing a base flag yields the distinguished generators ρ_0,...,ρ_{n-1} of Γ(P), and Γ(P) is a string C-group: it is generated by involutions satisfying the string commutation relations (ρ_iρ_j)^2 = 1 for |i-j|≥2, and it satisfies the intersection condition
   ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I⟩ ∩ ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ J⟩ = ⟨ρ_i : i ∈ I ∩ J⟩  for all I, J ⊆ {0,...,n-1}.
This intersection condition, together with the string relations, exactly characterizes which groups arise as automorphism groups of regular abstract polytopes.

Problem. Let P be a k-orbit abstract n-polytope (k ≥ 2), and suppose one is given a distinguished generating set of Γ(P) (depending on a choice of base flags from each flag orbit and reflecting the symmetry type graph of P) that plays the role analogous to the distinguished generators ρ_0,...,ρ_{n-1} in the regular case. Determine the precise combinatorial/group-theoretic condition on these generators — replacing the string C-group intersection condition — that is necessary and sufficient for a group with such a generating set to be the automorphism group of an abstract polytope of the prescribed symmetry type, i.e. such that this generator data faithfully recovers the polytope.
artifact.status_search_result: Partial answers exist. For 3-orbit polyhedra, explicit necessary and sufficient generator/intersection conditions have been worked out (Cunningham–Pellicer, J. Algebraic Combin., 2022). A general framework realizing every abstract n-polytope as a coset geometry, giving generators, relations, and intersection-type conditions tied to the symmetry type graph, was developed by Hubard et al. ("All polytopes are coset geometries", 2022/2023). A single clean uniform analogue of the string C-group intersection condition for arbitrary k-orbit polytopes, however, is not fully settled in the literature.

status_evidence.title: All polytopes are coset geometries: Characterizing automorphism groups of k-orbit abstract polytopes
status_evidence.snippet: Characterizing, in terms of generators, relations and intersection conditions, the automorphism group of a k-orbit polytope with given symmetry type graph.
status_evidence.claim: A general characterization of k-orbit polytope automorphism groups via generators, relations and intersection conditions has been formulated.

status_evidence.title: Automorphism groups of 3-orbit polyhedra
status_evidence.snippet: Necessary and sufficient conditions on a set of generators of a group Γ in order to construct a polyhedron in which Γ acts having 3 orbits on flags.
status_evidence.claim: For 3-orbit polyhedra, the analogue of the intersection condition has been determined.
